## International partners

### Delft University of Technology {#tudelft}

**Faculty of Civil Engineering and Geosciences · Netherlands**
With **Jan Rots** and **Rita Esposito**.

A single line of work on the mechanics of masonry, from the modelling strategy
down to the material that decays. It covers block-based and full-scale
approaches to unreinforced masonry, the damage that seismic vibrations induce
between building components, and the long-term side of the same problem:
weathering, salt crystallisation and multiphase hygro-thermal modelling of
historic materials and masonry quay walls.

Selected joint work:

| Year | |
|---|---|
| 2025 | Salt crystallisation and weathering in masonry retaining walls: a multiphase modelling approach |
| 2025 | Numerical simulation of long-term effects of weathering due to salt crystallisation on masonry quay walls |
| 2020 | Modeling strategies for the computational analysis of unreinforced masonry structures |
| 2019 | A damaging block-based model for the cyclic behaviour of full-scale masonry structures |
| 2019 | A review of numerical models for masonry structures |

: {tbl-colwidths="[10,90]"}

### ISISE — University of Minho {#isise}

**Institute for Sustainability and Innovation in Structural Engineering · Portugal**
With **Paulo B. Lourenço**, **Daniel V. Oliveira** and **Miguel Azenha**.

Masonry, composite strengthening and BIM. The work spans experimental and
numerical techniques for masonry products and earthquake engineering,
strengthening methods with composite materials, and BIM-supported data
management for historical constructions — including IoT workflows, low-cost
LiDAR survey and the transformation of point clouds into models that both the
structural analysis and the building information model can use.

Selected joint work:

| Year | |
|---|---|
| 2025 | Streamlining FE and BIM modeling for historic buildings with point cloud transformation |
| 2023 | Investigating the seismic response of URM walls with irregular opening layout through different modelling approaches |

: {tbl-colwidths="[10,90]"}

### University of California San Diego {#ucsd}

**Jacobs School of Engineering · United States**
With **Petr Krysl**.

The longest-running of these collaborations, begun during two post-doctoral
years at UCSD and still active: shell and plate elements, and locking-free
displacement formulations with nodal integration. Twelve joint papers to date,
the most recent in 2026.

Selected joint work:

| Year | |
|---|---|
| 2026 | A robust quadrilateral Reissner–Mindlin shell element with six degrees of freedom per node |
| 2015 | Linear tetrahedral element for problems of plastic deformation |
| 2014 | Assumed-strain nodally integrated hexahedral element for elastoplastic applications |
| 2009 | Displacement-based finite elements with nodal integration for Reissner–Mindlin plates |

: {tbl-colwidths="[10,90]"}

The full list is on the [publications page](publications.qmd).

## Collaboration themes

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### Heritage structures

Digital-twin workflows, survey-to-model pipelines, masonry diagnostics and
decision support for conservation.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### Computational mechanics

Finite element and virtual element formulations, nonlinear response and robust
open-source implementation.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### Sustainable materials

Bio-based and recycled materials, experimental characterization and numerical
modelling for building applications.
:::

:::
